machine_learning: The bias-variance tradeoff states that the expected test error can be decomposed into bias squared, variance, and irreducible error.
Overfitting occurs when a model learns the training data too well, including noise, resulting in poor generalization to new data.
Cross-validation is a technique used to assess how well a model generalizes by partitioning data into training and validation sets.
The curse of dimensionality refers to various phenomena that arise when analyzing data in high-dimensional spaces.
Regularization techniques like L1 and L2 add penalty terms to the loss function to prevent overfitting.
Bagging reduces variance by training multiple models on different subsets of the training data and averaging their predictions.
Boosting reduces bias by sequentially training weak learners, where each subsequent learner focuses on the mistakes of previous ones.
The no free lunch theorem states that no single machine learning algorithm works best for every problem.
Feature scaling normalizes input features to have similar ranges, improving the performance of distance-based algorithms.
The training error typically decreases as model complexity increases, while validation error first decreases then increases.
Ensemble methods combine multiple models to create a stronger predictor than any individual model alone.
The VC dimension measures the capacity of a hypothesis class to shatter sets of points.
Early stopping prevents overfitting by halting training when validation error starts to increase.
Data augmentation artificially increases the size of training datasets by applying transformations to existing samples.
deep_learning: Backpropagation computes gradients of the loss function with respect to network weights using the chain rule.
The vanishing gradient problem occurs when gradients become exponentially small in deep networks, making training difficult.
ReLU activation functions help mitigate the vanishing gradient problem by providing non-zero gradients for positive inputs.
Batch normalization normalizes inputs to each layer, accelerating training and improving stability.
Dropout randomly sets a fraction of input units to zero during training to prevent overfitting.
Convolutional layers use shared weights and local connectivity to efficiently process grid-like data such as images.
Pooling layers reduce spatial dimensions while retaining important features in convolutional neural networks.
LSTM networks use gating mechanisms to selectively remember and forget information over long sequences.
The universal approximation theorem states that feedforward networks with sufficient hidden units can approximate any continuous function.
Transfer learning leverages pre-trained models on related tasks to improve performance on new tasks with limited data.
Gradient descent optimization updates model parameters in the direction of steepest descent of the loss function.
The exploding gradient problem occurs when gradients become exponentially large, causing unstable training.
Residual connections allow gradients to flow directly through skip connections, enabling training of very deep networks.
Attention mechanisms allow models to focus on relevant parts of the input when making predictions.
probability_statistics: Bayes' theorem relates conditional probabilities: P(A|B) = P(B|A) × P(A) / P(B).
The Central Limit Theorem states that the sampling distribution of sample means approaches a normal distribution as sample size increases.
The Law of Large Numbers states that sample averages converge to the expected value as the number of trials increases.
A probability distribution assigns probabilities to all possible outcomes of a random experiment.
The expected value of a random variable is the weighted average of all possible values, weighted by their probabilities.
Variance measures the spread of a probability distribution around its mean.
Independent events satisfy the condition P(A ∩ B) = P(A) × P(B).
A confidence interval provides a range of plausible values for a population parameter with a specified confidence level.
The p-value is the probability of observing test results at least as extreme as the observed results, assuming the null hypothesis is true.
Maximum likelihood estimation finds parameter values that maximize the likelihood of observing the given data.
The binomial distribution models the number of successes in a fixed number of independent Bernoulli trials.
The normal distribution is characterized by its bell-shaped curve and is completely determined by its mean and variance.
Correlation measures the linear relationship between two variables, ranging from -1 to 1.
The chi-square test assesses whether observed frequencies differ significantly from expected frequencies.
linear_algebra: A matrix is invertible if and only if its determinant is non-zero.
Eigenvalues are scalars λ such that Av = λv for some non-zero vector v, where A is a square matrix.
The rank of a matrix is the dimension of the vector space spanned by its columns.
Orthogonal matrices preserve lengths and angles, satisfying the condition Q^T Q = I.
The trace of a square matrix is the sum of its diagonal elements.
Singular Value Decomposition factorizes any matrix A as A = UΣV^T, where U and V are orthogonal matrices.
The null space of a matrix A consists of all vectors x such that Ax = 0.
Linear independence means that no vector in a set can be expressed as a linear combination of the others.
The determinant of a matrix gives the scaling factor of the linear transformation it represents.
Principal Component Analysis finds the directions of maximum variance in high-dimensional data.
The Gram-Schmidt process orthogonalizes a set of linearly independent vectors.
A basis for a vector space is a linearly independent set that spans the entire space.
The column space of a matrix A consists of all possible linear combinations of its column vectors.
Positive definite matrices have all positive eigenvalues and define convex quadratic functions.
